turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack what sort of an address it was, and if it was in the more fashionable part of the square.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was uncertain about the exact part of Belgrave Square but assured her that it was a respectable address.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he had a clear idea of the social standing of his acquaintances, and whether he was acquainted with any of the nobility.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that while he was not personally acquainted with the nobility, he was acquainted with many individuals of good standing and respectable families.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he had any connections with any of the prominent families of the county, insisting on the importance of such ties in the assessment of a potential suitor.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she could not understand why social connections were more important than personal qualities.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was unimpressed with mere acquaintances and pressed him on whether he had any substantial ties to influential families.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that although he did not come from a noble lineage, he was committed to establishing a respectable and influential network within society.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that social standing was more than just personal ambition and that she required evidence of established connections and influence.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she could not see the point in dismissing a man based on his lack of social connections when his character and intentions were much more significant.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that Gwendolen should not concern herself with such matters and told Jack that she would not be swayed by personal qualities alone; she required concrete evidence of social and financial stability.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he understood her concerns and assured her that he would do everything in his power to acquire the connections and influence that she valued.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was not easily convinced by mere assurances and required tangible proof of his social standing and financial stability before she would consider approving of their engagement.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood Lady Bracknell’s skepticism and told her that he would work diligently to provide the evidence she sought, assuring her of his commitment and sincerity.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she appreciated his commitment but reminded him that actions spoke louder than words, and she would need to see proof of his social and financial advancement before she would give her consent to their engagement.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded respectfully and told Lady Bracknell that he understood the importance of concrete evidence and would make every effort to provide her with the necessary proofs of his social standing and financial stability.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she expected him to present his case to her again in a month, at which time she would be in a position to make a more informed decision.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded respectfully and told Lady Bracknell that he would work tirelessly to meet her expectations and provide the necessary evidence of his social standing and financial stability within the month.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that Jack must ensure his evidence was impeccable and that she would not be swayed by empty promises or half-hearted efforts.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded again and told Lady Bracknell that he would do everything in his power to ensure that the evidence he presented was impeccable and would meet her high standards.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell that she was engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she was not engaged to anyone and that when she did become engaged, she or her father would inform her of the fact.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell, 'Mamma!'

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to go to the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to get into the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack to take a seat.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he preferred standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she felt bound to inform him that he was not down on her list of eligible young men.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he must admit he smoked.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was glad to hear it and that a man should always have an occupation of some kind.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he knew everything or nothing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he knew nothing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was pleased to hear it and that she did not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if his income was in land or in investments.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was in investments.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that it was satisfactory.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he had a country house with some land attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that a country house was satisfactory and asked how many bedrooms it had.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned a house in Belgrave Square, but it was let by the year to Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she did not know Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that Lady Bloxham went about very little and was a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that nowadays that was no guarantee of respectability of character and asked what number in Belgrave Square.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that the number was 149.
